subject: Econ launch: Canary playbook and guardrails for routing/quant
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@datascale.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.k@meridiancloud.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Econ launch: Canary playbook and guardrails for routing/quant

Morning team,

Putting the canary playbook into this thread so we have one source-of-truth for launch controls. Objective: validate cost/perf tradeoffs in production-like conditions and leave safe rollbacks/guardrails in place. Key success criteria: P95 <= 420ms for support-bot (1k concurrent), per-generated-token cost <= $0.0019 for support-bot, no >1% regression in doc-summarize ROUGE on canary traffic.

Top-level plan (see attachment canary-playbook.md):
- Canary scope: 10% of traffic for support-bot; 100% isolation for doc-summarize on int8 pinned variant.
- Batching window: start 25ms (canary) -> evaluate 25 vs 50ms impact.
- Cache strategy: KV-prefetch warmup for doc-summarize; prefix caching for top 50 document hashes. TTL initially 7 days.
- Quant mapping: support-bot -> int4-mixed with cost-aware fallback to int8 if confidence < threshold; doc-summarize -> int8 pinned.
- Observability: per-request model token breakdown, request score/confidence, and a loss-of-consistency alert if content divergence > threshold.

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik: publish the batching test scaffold and enable per-model token counters in traces for the canary. ETA EOD today?
2) Monica: confirm the list of top-50 document hashes and long-prefix thresholds.
3) Alex/Priya: confirm you can route 10% of prod-like traffic to the Redwood canary pool Wed 6/30 10:00-13:00 PT and allow trace collection.

Attachments: canary-playbook.md (text/markdown), batching-results-20270630.csv (csv stub), observability-dashboards.png (image/png).

I will run the kickoff sync at 10:05 PT right before the generator window. If we see any red flags in the first 30 minutes we rollback to 0% immediately.

Hannah
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@datascale.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.k@meridiancloud.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Econ launch: Canary playbook and guardrails for routing/quant

Thanks Hannah 5 quick status and some engineering guardrails: 

- Batching test scaffold: prepared. I can run parallel buckets for 25ms vs 50ms and produce P50/P95, CPU/GPU utilization, and per-token cost breakdown. I need the generator artifact from Meridian for the 1k-concurrency shape (Alex, thanks in advance). ETA to produce initial CSV is today 14:30 PT.
- Token breakdown: will emit model_variant_token_count and a derived cost column per request. Ill also add a flag in traces for "quant_fallback_triggered" so we can track fallback frequency.
- Canary rollout plan (short): start 10% traffic, evaluate first 30 minutes for latency and fallback rate; if fallback rate > 8% or P95 > 480ms rollback. If errors spike > 0.5% rollback.

One technical question: for support-bot we plan int4-mixed + cost-aware fallback. Do we want the fallback to be immediate on low-confidence or allow a grace window (e.g., try int4, if confidence below threshold AND response length > X then replay to int8)? A replay increases user latency but reduces bad outputs. Recommend: allow immediate fallback for admin flows only, otherwise record and replay asynchronously for user-visible flows. Need Monica's mapping of which flows care about immediate correctness.

I'll attach the initial CSV to Drive when done (batching-results-20270630.csv).

5Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@datascale.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.k@meridiancloud.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Econ launch: Canary playbook and guardrails for routing/quant

Quick validations from prompt sampling and prefix analysis: 
- Confirmed top-50 doc hashes (sheet in Drive). These account for ~72% of doc-summarize calls; KV-prefetch warmup will give strong tail benefits.
- Flow classification for fallback policy:
  * support-bot (chat support) 5 low-cost tolerant, ok with async replay for edge cases
  * billing-admin (admin queries) 5 strict correctness, immediate fallback to int8 required
  * doc-summarize 5 pinned int8 as discussed

I agree with Karthik's replay suggestion: allow async replay for support-bot when fallback triggers, surface original response with a short disclaimer and update via webhook when corrected. For billing-admin do immediate sync fallback. I'll drop the flow mapping into the canary-playbook.md and the Drive sheet.

Monica
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: flow-mapping.csv (in Drive)
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@datascale.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@meridiancloud.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Econ launch: Canary playbook and guardrails for routing/quant

All good from Meridian infra side. We will spin up the 1k-concurrency generator and route 10% of prod-like traffic into the Redwood canary pool on Thu 7/1 10:00-13:00 PT. A few asks from our end: 

- Please include model_variant_token_count and quant_fallback_triggered in the exported CSV so our finance and risk teams can reconcile.
- Can you include a short JSON field in traces with the canary-id and rollout-phase so we can tag our logs?
- If you plan any replay behavior, document the webhook pattern and expected latency so our UI team can handle the update flow.

We'll accept the calendar invite and upload the generator artifact to the Drive folder by EOD today.

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
Senior SRE, Meridian Cloud
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Alex Nguyen <alex@datascale.ai>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@meridiancloud.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 14:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Econ launch: Canary playbook and guardrails for routing/quant

Thanks everyone 5 finalizing the playbook and timeline:

- Generator window confirmed Thu 7/1 10:00-13:00 PT. Karthik will upload batching-results-20270630.csv and the per-request token breakdown to Drive within 2 hours of the run.
- Monica to publish flow-mapping and webhook contract in Drive by EOD Fri 7/2.
- Observability: Karthik will add the canary-id and rollout-phase JSON tag to traces; Alex will verify on his side.
- Rollback thresholds: fallback rate > 8% OR P95 > 480ms OR error rate > 0.5% -> immediate rollback to 0%.

I'll follow up after the run with a short post-mortem summary and the canary metrics. If all looks good we'll scale from 10%->50% over 48 hours with the same guardrails.

Hannah
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: canary-playbook.md (final draft)
